multipleTestingNote: 8 pre-registered event(s) x 7 horizons = 56 cells screened. P-values are NOT corrected for multiple testing; treat a single green cell among many as weak evidence.

events.name: GLD oversold washout below its 200-day SMA
events.rationale: A mean-reversion proxy, NOT a replication of the SentimenTrader GLD study (which rests on a proprietary Optix sentiment index and a 21-year seasonal window we cannot reproduce). Mechanism: a liquid, widely-held commodity ETF that becomes acutely oversold (RSI below 30) while already trading below its 200-day SMA has usually overshot on momentum or forced selling, so a partial snap-back toward the mean is common over the following weeks. Deliberately a COUNTER-TREND test, logged as such, not a trend signal. Forward returns on GLD; significance from our random-entry Monte Carlo; thin-sample caveat applies.
events.definition: Trigger on the session GLD's RSI(14) crosses below 30 while GLD closes below its 200-day SMA. Forward returns measured on GLD from the trigger close.
events.entryNote: Forward return measured from the close of the trigger day (event-study convention).

events.name: SLV oversold washout below its 200-day SMA
events.rationale: The same oversold-in-downtrend mean-reversion construct as the GLD card, applied to silver to test whether the washout-bounce holds across precious metals. Silver (SLV) is higher-beta and more volatile than gold, so washouts run deeper and snap-backs are larger but noisier; the natural robustness check on the gold result. Counter-trend by design. Forward returns on SLV; significance from our random-entry Monte Carlo; thin-sample caveat applies.
events.definition: Trigger on the session SLV's RSI(14) crosses below 30 while SLV closes below its 200-day SMA. Forward returns measured on SLV from the trigger close.
events.entryNote: Forward return measured from the close of the trigger day (event-study convention).

events.name: LIT oversold washout below its 200-day SMA
events.rationale: The same oversold-in-downtrend mean-reversion construct as the GLD and SLV cards, extended to LIT (Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF) — a high-beta thematic ETF that has spent years in a deep drawdown. Prompted by a SentimenTrader note on depressed lithium sentiment, but deliberately NOT their study: their signal is a proprietary Optix sentiment composite, and their headline was a cross-asset LIT-to-gold/stocks curiosity that the author himself concedes has no mechanism and frames as weight-of-evidence rather than a buy signal. We test only the reproducible, mechanism-having piece — does a washed-out thematic ETF partially mean-revert — on our own price data, and drop the cross-asset angle entirely. Counter-trend by design; single-sector concentration and LIT's short history (2010 inception, ~10y of daily data here) make this the thinnest-sample washout on the book. Forward returns on LIT; significance from our random-entry Monte Carlo; thin-sample caveat applies. OUR RESULT: on this data the LIT washout does NOT bounce — it is a value trap. Short-term continuation is significantly negative (1-to-2-week medians around -2 to -3%, p < 0.05) and the 1-year median is about -8% at a 25% hit rate. Retained as the honest counter-example — the precious-metals washout mechanism does not generalise to a single-theme ETF in a structural downtrend, and it is a live reminder that 'oversold' is not 'cheap'.
events.definition: Trigger on the session LIT's RSI(14) crosses below 30 while LIT closes below its 200-day SMA. Forward returns measured on LIT from the trigger close.
events.entryNote: Forward return measured from the close of the trigger day (event-study convention).

events.name: S&P 500 strong 2nd quarter → 9-month forward
events.rationale: A strong second quarter — a price gain in each of April, May and June, and/or a quarterly price gain of 10 per cent or more from the end of March to the end of June — is a momentum-and-participation regime signal. Broad, sustained strength into mid-year has historically been followed by above-base-rate S&P 500 price returns over the following nine months (June close to the following March close). This is not a replication of the SentimenTrader record, which is a proprietary lead re-tested here on our own data; the card reports OUR numbers only. The honest edge is the excess over the unconditional nine-month base rate — the S&P 500 is already positive over roughly four in five nine-month windows — not the raw win rate, and signals cluster in secular bull markets, so the effective sample is thinner than the raw count. A long-only seasonal context signal, judged on our random-entry Monte Carlo, with a thin-sample caveat carried on the card.
events.definition: At each June month-end, flag a 'strong' 2nd quarter when the S&P 500 posts a price gain in each of April, May and June, and/or gains 10% or more from the end of March to the end of June. Forward returns measured on the S&P 500 price index from the June close over 3/6/9/12 months (9M is the headline: June close to the following March close).
events.entryNote: Forward return measured on the monthly price index from the June month-end close (event-study convention).

events.name: China ETF breadth recovery from a drawdown
events.rationale: Prompted by a SentimenTrader note on a Hang Seng breadth thrust, rebuilt on our OWN data — and deliberately NOT their signal. Theirs is the percentage of Hang Seng CONSTITUENTS above their moving averages; we hold no Hong Kong equities (Norgate carries none), so this is a PROXY: segment-level breadth across a basket of ~11 US-listed China/HK ETFs spanning A-shares, offshore large-cap, and internet/tech. Mechanism: a broad participation recovery — the share of the China complex back above its 50-day average crossing up through 55% while the market is still 18% or more below its one-year high — signals that a washed-out market is being bought across segments, which has historically tended to precede continuation rather than a fresh leg down. Three honest caveats carried on the card: (1) ETF-segment breadth is COARSER than constituent breadth (~11 items, not dozens of names); (2) the basket is US-listed and therefore USD-denominated, so the currency layer sits on top; (3) the ~10-year daily window here yields only a handful of independent episodes — a thin sample. Target: FXI (HK large-cap China, the closest liquid proxy to the Hang Seng). Significance from our random-entry Monte Carlo. OUR RESULT: on this thin proxy the recovery produces only a mild short-term pop (1-week to 1-month medians around +1 to +2%) that fades to a NEGATIVE edge at 2-to-3 months, and is not statistically significant at any horizon — no sign of the strong medium-term continuation the lead described, and consistent with the tendency of Chinese equities to roll over quickly after participation spikes. A deeper ADR-level breadth basket, survivorship-clean via Norgate, is a possible future upgrade that might sharpen what this coarse 11-ETF basket cannot resolve.
events.definition: Trigger when the percentage of a ~11-ETF China basket (A-shares, offshore large-cap, internet/tech) trading above their own 50-day SMA crosses up through 55%, while FXI is at least 18% below its trailing 252-day high. Forward returns measured on FXI from the trigger close.
events.entryNote: Forward return measured from the close of the trigger day (event-study convention).

events.name: KOSPI panic breadth — % at 12-week lows spikes above 80%
events.rationale: SURVIVORSHIP CAVEAT, FRONT AND CENTRE: this breadth is computed over EWY's CURRENT ~55 large/mid KOSPI holdings, NOT point-in-time membership — names that delisted or dropped out are absent, which biases historical breadth-health upward and understates past panics. Treat the record as indicative, not survivorship-clean; a clean version needs a paid international-constituents feed or a forward daily-capture database. Rebuilt on our OWN data from a SentimenTrader KOSPI lead (Korean constituent breadth we could not otherwise compute). Mechanism: when 80% or more of the basket simultaneously prints a fresh 12-week low (first such spike in six months), the selloff has reached a fear/capitulation extreme, and such extremes have historically tended to precede a bounce — a 'prepare to buy', NOT a 'buy': acting immediately is catching a falling knife, so wait for price confirmation before committing capital. Target EWY (the USD-tradable Korea proxy, ~80-90% correlated to the KOSPI). Rare by construction, so the sample is minuscule — both the vendor and we flag it as too small to draw firm conclusions. Significance from our random-entry Monte Carlo. OUR RESULT: on full 2005+ history the extreme has fired only TWICE — the 2008 GFC bottom (24 Oct 2008) and the COVID crash (13 Mar 2020) — both generational V-bottoms after which EWY rose roughly 100% over the following year. n=2 is an anecdote, not evidence (the low Monte-Carlo p-values are not meaningful at this sample), so the credibility gate correctly marks this IGNORE. As of 2026-07-30 the reading is about 18% at 12-week lows, far below the 80% trigger: the KOSPI has cratered but NOT capitulated, matching the source lead.
events.definition: Trigger when the percentage of the KOSPI basket (EWY's current large/mid holdings) printing a fresh 60-day (~12-week) low crosses up through 80%, de-clustered to the first such spike in any 126-session (~6-month) window. Forward returns measured on EWY from the trigger close.
events.entryNote: Forward return measured from the close of the trigger day (event-study convention).

events.name: Copper/Gold ratio extreme-low → copper
events.rationale: Prompted by a SentimenTrader copper/gold lead, rebuilt on OUR data with OUR threshold. Mechanism: the copper/gold ratio is a classic growth-vs-safe-haven gauge — copper is an industrial-demand bellwether, gold a haven — so an extreme LOW (copper cheap relative to gold) marks maximal pessimism on global growth, which has historically mean-reverted with copper rallying. We use Norgate's #CUGC ratio (1993+) and trigger when it falls into the bottom 12% of its FULL history (a descriptive, disclosed in-sample threshold — never the vendor's fixed 0.16, which is units-dependent; an expanding/causal threshold DRIFTS on this bimodal ratio and manufactures spurious crossings, so it was rejected), de-clustered to the first extreme in 12 months. Target: CPER (the clean investable copper ETF; COPX copper-miners would be a higher-beta alternative). HONEST CAVEATS: (1) CPER only starts 2011, so the sample is TINY — the 2008 GFC extreme is excluded and only about three completed episodes remain; (2) like the LIT-Optix re-test, this is really a GENERALISED growth-pessimism-washout signal — the extremes are macro bottoms (2016, 2020, 2024), so a clean record is a handful of once-a-cycle buys, not a dense edge; (3) copper-futures roll is avoided by using CPER, though CPER's own roll cost applies. Significance from our random-entry Monte Carlo. The term-structure leg of the source note (HG1/HG6 futures curve) is data-gated and omitted. OUR RESULT: on CPER (2011+) the signal fires three times (2016, 2019, 2024) — copper's 12-month return was +18.5% median, 3/3 positive, versus a +0.4% base, but with an interim ~6-month soft patch (the note's '5-7% drawdown first'); n=3 is an anecdote and the credibility gate IGNOREs it.
events.definition: Trigger when the copper/gold ratio (Norgate #CUGC) falls into the bottom 12% of its full history, the first such extreme in 12 months. Forward returns measured on CPER (copper) from the trigger month-end close over 3/6/12 months (12M is the headline).
events.entryNote: Forward returns measured on the target from the trigger month-end close (event-study convention).

events.name: Copper/Gold ratio extreme-low → S&P 500
events.rationale: The macro companion to the copper card, on the SAME trigger: when the copper/gold ratio hits an extreme low (bottom 12% of its full history, first in 12 months — our own percentile threshold, not the vendor's 0.16), what happens to the S&P 500? Mechanism: an extreme-low copper/gold reflects a global-growth fear washout, and such risk-off extremes have historically been contrarian-bullish for equities as the pessimism mean-reverts. Rebuilt on OUR data — Norgate #CUGC ratio (1993+) as the trigger, S&P 500 price index (Norgate $SPX) as the target, so this card sees EVERY trigger since 1993 (the larger, more honest sample of the two copper cards). CAVEAT: the extremes still cluster at a handful of macro bottoms (GFC, 2016, COVID, 2024), so treat the win rate as a small number of generational risk-off buys, not a dense timing edge — the same generalised-washout character as the copper card and the LIT-Optix re-test. Significance from our random-entry Monte Carlo. OUR RESULT: the ratio hit this extreme four times since 1993 (2008, 2016, 2019, 2024) — the S&P 500's 12-month return was +21.0% median, 4/4 positive, versus a +10.9% base (a ~+10pp edge); n=4 keeps it below significance (p=0.18), and the win rate is four generational risk-off buys, not a dense timing edge.
events.definition: Trigger when the copper/gold ratio (Norgate #CUGC) falls into the bottom 12% of its full history, the first such extreme in 12 months. Forward returns measured on the S&P 500 price index from the trigger month-end close over 3/6/12 months.
events.entryNote: Forward returns measured on the target from the trigger month-end close (event-study convention).
